item.description:
A pass over the things only the person who wrote Changmun would know, and the habits you bring from other browsers.
- **Nothing lost without a word:** quitting asks while files still download; pages with unsaved changes ask before you leave; an AI question you don't answer in 90 seconds counts as Don't Allow and says so; Stop keeps the messages that were waiting; ⇧⌘T brings closed tabs back after a restart too (Clear History removes them). - **Moving around:** right-click ‹ or › for the page history, ⌘. or Esc to stop loading, ⌘← / ⌘→ to go back and forward when the page doesn't use those keys, ⌘R retries a page that failed, ⌥-click downloads a link, and Develop › View Page Source (⌥⌘U). - **Tabs:** ⌘⇧[ ⌘⇧] and ⌘1–9 follow the whole sidebar; middle-click closes a tab; Close Other Tabs and Close Tabs Below; Undo after closing a tab; Move to Space; a "…" menu on every tab row; favorites and bookmarks show and mute their sound. - **Said in words:** "Not Secure" on http pages, "Camera on" while a page uses it (click to stop), the AI button says Working or Answered with its panel closed, and sleeping or background tabs say so. - **Easier to find:** a Help menu with the guide and every shortcut (⌘/), Settings search that finds every setting, and a first-run screen that shows the search bar, spaces and approvals. - **New:** notifications when a download finishes or the AI waits while you're in another app, the download count on the Dock icon, Share and Services, your own search engines with a keyword, and bookmarks exported to or imported from an HTML file.
Tried with 1611 automated tests and the off-screen test copy. Dragging, hover and notification prompts were not tried on a real screen yet.

- **Changed:** when a page is waiting on you (a pop-up it was refused, a password to save, an extension to install), the left of the address now says so in words, such as "Pop-up Blocked", instead of showing a small dot that didn't say what it was. Press it for the same choices as before, such as "Always Allow for This Site".
Tried with automated tests and the off-screen test copy, on a page that opens an empty window from a timer the way older in-house systems do.

- **Fixed:** when a site opened an empty window without a click and filled it in itself, as many older in-house and school systems do, Changmun blocked it without telling you, so there was no way to let it through and the site just failed. Now the dot beside the address tells you about it, with "Always Allow for This Site"; allow it and press the site's button again.
Tried with automated tests on a page that opens an empty window from a timer. The in-house system this came up on hasn't been tried, so tell me if its window still doesn't open.

- **Back:** a video playing in a tab you leave floats in Picture in Picture again, like in Arc, and goes back into its tab when you return. It was taken out in 0.15.0 to trim settings; it is on by default, and Settings › Tabs › "Play video in Picture in Picture when you switch to another tab" turns it off.
Tried with the automated tests. Picture in Picture opens a window on screen, which the off-screen test copy can't do, so the float itself hasn't been watched; tell me if a video doesn't float when you switch tabs.

- **Fixed:** on Olive Young, adding an item to the cart no longer shows the "added to cart" layer. Ad blocking stopped the Kakao pixel's script, and the shop's own code calls that pixel without checking that it is there, so it failed before it could open the layer. That one script now loads on Olive Young alone; what the pixel would send (its events, ad ID and third-party cookie check) stays blocked there too, and nothing changes on other sites. The rules are rebuilt the next time you open Changmun.
Tried with automated tests and the headless copy, by replaying the shop's add-to-cart step on a test page. A real cart on a logged-in account hasn't been tried, so tell me if the layer is still missing.

- **A new app icon.** The window is drawn as a sign: the arch, one upright and one crossbar, all in a single stroke, in two colours. The light on the floor, its shadow and the gradient on the tile are gone. It reads at 32 pixels, on a light Dock and on a dark one.
Tried with automated tests and a render of the icon on both Docks. An icon that changes with the system's light and dark look isn't in this version: I couldn't confirm on my Mac that macOS draws it.

- **One layout.** Tabs live in the sidebar, the toolbar sits above the page, and the address is the pill. The settings that moved these around, tabs on top, toolbar in the sidebar, address bar position and sidebar width, are gone, along with the tab strip they needed. If you had tabs on top, they are back in the sidebar. - **Notices in one place.** A saved-login offer, a blocked pop-up and a Web Store install no longer stack as bars over the page. A dot at the left of the address shows there is something waiting, and one list behind it holds them, with the same choices as before. - **A plainer start page.** A search field and your favorites, on a plain background. The three start page styles, the extra sections, the background picture and the shortcut hints are gone. - **Downloads in words.** A running download reads "name · 42% · Downloading" and a finished one "name · 2.1 MB · Done", in the sidebar, and a finished one stays until you close it. With the sidebar hidden, the percentage shows beside the downloads button. The progress ring and the dot are gone. - **No accent in the chrome.** The AI button, the working indicator and the space name are plain ink. - **Fewer settings.** Developer Mode, Picture in Picture on tab switch and automatic grouping of new tabs are gone; the rest stays. - **Fixed:** the certificate warning was hard to see in light mode; the shield and star beside the address can now be reached from the keyboard and VoiceOver; the remove buttons in Settings have names for VoiceOver; the "Update password?" question had a Save button; a few Korean particles and the words for Delete and Remove were inconsistent.
This follows Dieter Rams's "less, but better": settings that chose where things go are gone, and one place holds each thing. Tried with automated tests and the headless copy. The settings you lose come back at their defaults; tell me if one you relied on is missing.

- **Downloads in one place.** With the sidebar showing, the downloads button now sits in its bottom bar, right under the shelf where a download's progress appears, so the list opens where you saw it come in instead of at the other end of the window. With the tabs on top or the sidebar hidden, the button stays beside the address.
Tried with automated tests and the headless copy.

- **Fixed:** the key button that fills a saved login didn't appear on sites whose scripts draw the sign-in form after the page has loaded, Coupang among them. The page was looked at once, when it finished loading, and the form wasn't there yet. The button now comes when the password field appears, and goes when the field goes.
Tried with automated tests and the headless copy. Coupang's own sign-in page hasn't been tried by hand, so tell me if the key is still missing there.

- **Fixed:** sites with a bot check, such as Coupang, could refuse to show search results or other pages. Changmun used to replace the page's `window.open` to notice pop-ups it had refused, and a bot check that reads the browser's own functions saw the replacement and took the browser for a bot. Refused pop-ups are now noticed from the app's own decision, so the page's functions stay the browser's own. The bar that offers a refused pop-up works as before; the warning in the page's console is gone.
Tried with automated tests and the headless copy. Whether Coupang now shows results hasn't been tried by hand, so tell me if it still refuses.
